notes.text: A flaw was found in Vim, a widely used command-line text editor. This vulnerability allows a local attacker to execute arbitrary code on the system. By opening a specially crafted Python file and then triggering the omni-completion feature, the attacker can cause Vim to run malicious code from a sibling Python package. This could lead to a complete compromise of the user's system.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: vim: Vim: Arbitrary code execution via Python omni-completion
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important vulnerability in Vim that allows a local attacker to achieve arbitrary code execution. The flaw occurs when a user opens a specially crafted Python file and invokes omni-completion, leading to the execution of malicious code from a co-located Python package. This risk is present in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and other products where Vim is deployed with Python omni-completion enabled, potentially compromising the editing user's system.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: For more information visit https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2026:82061

Users can mitigate this vulnerability by disabling Python omni-completion in Vim if it is not essential for their workflow. This prevents the execution of untrusted Python code when opening hostile files. To disable this feature, ensure that the `omnifunc` option in your Vim configuration (e.g., `~/.vimrc`) is not set to `pythoncomplete#Complete` or `python3complete#Complete`. Alternatively, users should avoid invoking omni-completion (`Ctrl-X Ctrl-O`) on Python files from untrusted sources. Disabling Python omni-completion may affect Python development functionality within Vim.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `acl` package, specifically within its `libacl` pathname-based functions. A local attacker could exploit this vulnerability by using a symbolic link to replace a pathname component. This could allow the attacker to redirect access control list (ACL) read or write operations to arbitrary files or directories, leading to unauthorized manipulation of ACLs and ultimately local privilege escalation.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: acl: Symlink traversal privilege escalation via libacl functions
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this flaw as Important because a local attacker who controls any component of a pathname processed by a privileged process using libacl can redirect ACL operations to arbitrary files. Exploitation requires local access with the ability to create symlinks in a directory that a privileged program later processes with acl_get_file() or acl_set_file(). In default RHEL and OpenShift CoreOS configurations, standard file permission settings limit where unprivileged users can create symlinks, reducing the practical attack surface. Programs that operate on user-supplied paths with elevated privileges are most at risk.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: For more information visit https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2026:82061

Restrict unprivileged users from creating symlinks in directories that privileged processes operate on with ACL commands. Where possible, use the fs.protected_symlinks sysctl (enabled by default on RHEL 7+), which prevents symlink following in world-writable sticky directories unless the owner of the symlink matches the owner of the target file or directory.

vulnerabilities.title: acl: Symlink traversal privilege escalation via libacl functions

notes.text: A flaw was found in Linux-PAM's `pam_userdb` module. This vulnerability, categorized as an Observable Timing Discrepancy (CWE-208), allows a local or network-adjacent attacker to recover plaintext passwords. By repeatedly attempting authentication and measuring response-timing differences during plaintext password comparison, an attacker can deduce the password. This flaw is exploitable when the `pam_userdb` module is configured to store and compare credentials in plaintext, which is not a default setting.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: linux-pam: Plaintext password recovery via timing discrepancy in pam_userdb module
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Moderate flaw in Linux-PAM's `pam_userdb` module allows a local or network-adjacent attacker to recover plaintext passwords through a timing discrepancy. This vulnerability requires the `pam_userdb` module to be explicitly configured to store and compare credentials in plaintext, which is not a default or recommended configuration in Red Hat Enterprise Linux environments. The impact is limited by the need for repeated authentication attempts and specific, non-default module configurations.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: For more information visit https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2026:82061

To mitigate this issue, administrators should ensure that the `pam_userdb` module is not configured to store or compare credentials in plaintext. Verify that `pam_userdb` is either configured with a strong cryptographic hashing method or, if not required, is disabled. Avoid using `crypt=none` or omitting the `crypt=` argument when configuring `pam_userdb`. If changes are made to PAM configuration files, services relying on PAM may need to be restarted for the changes to take effect.

vulnerabilities.title: linux-pam: Plaintext password recovery via timing discrepancy in pam_userdb module

notes.text: A flaw was found in GLib. A buffer over-read can occur in the g_regex_replace function when used with the `G_REGEX_RAW` compile flag and case-change replacement escapes because the string_append function processes matched substrings using UTF-8 functions that assume valid UTF-8 input, even when the string is treated as raw bytes. notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Any applications that use g_regex_replace() or g_regex_replace_eval() with the G_REGEX_RAW compile flag and allow user-controlled replacement strings containing case-change escapes (\u, \l, \U, \L) are vulnerable to this issue. This flaw can cause a buffer over-read of 1-5 bytes, leading to a minor information disclosure and a denial of service when the buffer over-read crosses a page boundary. Due to these reasons, this vulnerability has been rated with a moderate severity.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: For more information visit https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2026:82061

Removing the G_REGEX_RAW flag or hardcoding the replacement strings will completely neutralize this issue.

notes.text: A flaw was found in GLib. The D-Bus client-side implementation of the DBUS_COOKIE_SHA1 SASL authentication mechanism does not validate the cookie_context parameter received from the server. A malicious D-Bus server can supply a cookie_context containing path traversal sequences, causing the client to read an arbitrary file and exfiltrate sensitive data by verifying guessed file contents against a generated hash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: glib: path traversal in glib/gio/gdbusauthmechanismsha1.c via keyring_lookup_entry and mechanism_client_data_receive
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this flaw, an attacker must be in a position to perform a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack on the connection or operate a malicious server that the client connects to. Furthermore, extracting data requires an oracle attack (guessing and hashing), increasing the complexity of exploitation. However, if successful, this issue allows the exfiltration of sensitive secrets, such as SSH keys or API tokens, from the filesystem. Due to these reasons, this vulnerability has been rated with a moderate severity.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: For more information visit https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2026:82061

To mitigate this vulnerability, ensure that applications only connect to trusted D-Bus servers and operate within secure, isolated networks to prevent man-in-the-middle (MitM) attacks. If feasible, configuring the D-Bus connection to strictly require the EXTERNAL authentication mechanism and disabling DBUS_COOKIE_SHA1 will completely neutralize this issue.

notes.text: A flaw was found in vLLM, an inference and serving engine for large language models. An attacker can exploit this by submitting specially crafted video requests that force the use of the PyNvVideoCodec GPU decoder. This bypasses the engine's static GPU memory reservation, allowing the attacker to exhaust shared GPU memory. The consequence is a denial of service (DoS), leading to request failures or worker crashes.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: vllm: vLLM: GPU memory exhaustion via PyNvVideoCodec decode bypass
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A MODERATE severity denial-of-service flaw was found in vLLM, the inference and serving engine shipped in Red Hat AI Inference Server and in Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI) vLLM-based components. A remote attacker with privileges to submit requests to a video-capable GPU deployment where the PyNvVideoCodec GPU decoder is installed can send specially crafted video requests that set media_io_kwargs.video.video_backend to pynvvideocodec, forcing use of the PyNvVideoCodec decoder even when the startup configuration selected a software decoder. Because the engine reserves decoder memory only according to its static configuration, the request-selected decoder's CUDA context, decoder surfaces, and decoded-frame allocations are not removed from the KV-cache budget, allowing the attacker to exhaust shared GPU memory and cause request failures, worker crashes, or denial of service. Red Hat rated this flaw MODERATE with CVSS 3.1 score 6.5 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H), consistent with the upstream rating; the impact is limited to availability, with no confidentiality or integrity impact. Affected Red Hat AI Inference Server and OpenShift AI components are marked DEFER because Red Hat does not file trackers for MODERATE severity flaws with a CVSS score below 7.0; the fix is deferred to a future product update, and the residual risk is denial of service on deployments that accept video requests on GPU hardware with PyNvVideoCodec installed. Deployments that do not process video requests or do not have the PyNvVideoCodec decoder installed are not exposed to this attack path.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: For more information visit https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2026:82061

Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability. The upstream vLLM project addressed this flaw in version 0.28.0, while fixes for Red Hat AI Inference Server and Red Hat OpenShift AI are currently deferred. Exposure can be reduced by not installing the PyNvVideoCodec decoder in vLLM serving images, since exploitation requires that backend to be present.

notes.text: A flaw was found in vLLM. An authenticated API client can exploit derender endpoints by providing oversized GenerateResponse objects. These endpoints process the objects without enforcing output bounds or response-size limits. This can lead to excessive consumption of CPU and memory resources, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: vllm: vLLM: Denial of Service via unbounded token ID decoding
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate severity denial of service flaw was found in vLLM, the LLM inference and serving engine shipped in Red Hat AI Inference Server and Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI. The /v1/completions/derender and /v1/chat/completions/derender API endpoints accept caller-supplied GenerateResponse objects and process their generate_responses, choices, token_ids, prompt_logprobs, logprobs.content, top_logprobs, and routed_experts structures through OnlineDerenderer and tokenizer.decode before limits such as max_model_len, max_tokens, max_num_seqs, or response-size restrictions are enforced. As a result, an authenticated API client can submit oversized GenerateResponse objects and cause excessive CPU and memory consumption, potentially producing oversized responses and degrading or denying service for other users of the vLLM instance. The affected Red Hat AI Inference Server and Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI streams are currently marked for a deferred fix; until a remediated update is delivered, deployments that expose the vLLM API to lower-trust authenticated clients retain residual risk of resource-exhaustion attacks. Red Hat and upstream both rate this issue Moderate (CVSS 4.3, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L), reflecting the availability-only impact and the credentials required to exploit it.

- `~/.vim/after/ftplugin/zsh.vim`: `setlocal keywordprg=`

notes.text: A flaw was found in vLLM, an inference and serving engine for large language models. The MiMoV2OmniMultiModalProcessor component improperly handles attacker-controlled image and audio strings, bypassing security protections. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to perform Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and read arbitrary local files accessible to the vLLM process. Successful exploitation could lead to unauthorized access to internal network resources, cloud metadata, and sensitive local system files.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: vllm: vLLM: Server-Side Request Forgery and arbitrary file read via improper media processing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate severity flaw was found in the vLLM inference and serving engine as shipped in Red Hat AI Inference Server and Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI. The MiMoV2OmniMultiModalProcessor in vllm/transformers_utils/processors/mimo_v2_omni.py passes attacker-controlled image and audio strings through _fetch_image, requests.get, and Image.open instead of the MediaConnector, bypassing the allowed_media_domains and allowed_local_media_path protections. A remote attacker able to submit multimodal requests to a vLLM server can use crafted image or audio strings to make the server issue requests to attacker-chosen URLs (server-side request forgery) and read arbitrary local files accessible to the vLLM process, potentially exposing internal network resources, cloud metadata services, and sensitive local system files. The Red Hat severity of Moderate (CVSS 6.5) is consistent with the upstream assessment. All currently affected Red Hat product streams ship vLLM versions that contain this flaw, and the fix is deferred: the upstream fix has not yet been incorporated into the affected Red Hat AI Inference Server and RHEL AI streams, leaving deployments that accept untrusted multimodal input at residual risk of information disclosure through server-side requests and local file reads.

notes.text: A flaw was found in HTTPX2, a Python HTTP client. The `Request._prepare()` function can incorrectly add a `Content-Length` header to a request that already includes a `Transfer-Encoding` header. This conflict in HTTP framing headers can lead to request smuggling or connection desynchronization. This could allow an attacker to bypass security controls or interfere with network traffic.

notes.text: A flaw was found in httpcore2, a component used by HTTPX2. When a remote origin uses WebSocket Secure (wss) through a SOCKS5 proxy, httpcore2 fails to initiate Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption because its upgrade condition only recognizes HTTPS. This vulnerability allows an attacker controlling or observing the proxy path to intercept and read sensitive WebSocket traffic, including authentication details and data frames, as it is transmitted in plaintext. The attacker could also modify the traffic or impersonate the WebSocket server, leading to information disclosure and potential compromise of communication integrity.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity because it completely compromises confidentiality and integrity over intended encrypted channels, permitting network-adjacent or man-in-the-middle attackers to capture authentication credentials and tamper with session data. In Red Hat environments, exposure is limited to specific deployments where client services are explicitly configured to route WebSocket Secure (wss://) connections through a SOCKS5 proxy. Direct secure WebSocket connections as well as standard HTTPS traffic traversing SOCKS5 proxies are unaffected, as they negotiate TLS handshakes as expected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in httpx2, a Python HTTP client. The content decoders in httpx2 fully inflate compressed network chunks (such as gzip, deflate, br, or zstd) before yielding bounded pieces to the application. This can lead to a small compressed chunk expanding significantly in memory, for example, a 64 KiB chunk expanding to approximately 64 MiB. A remote attacker, by controlling or compromising a server, could exploit this vulnerability to cause severe memory pressure or out-of-memory process termination, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) for applications using httpx2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in vLLM. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit an input validation vulnerability by submitting negative token IDs to the /v1/embeddings and /pooling endpoints. This action triggers a CUDA device-side assertion, which poisons the GPU context and causes the engine to crash. Consequently, all subsequent requests will fail until the process is restarted, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: vllm: vLLM: Denial of Service via negative token ID input
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having an Important severity because an unauthenticated remote attacker can completely disrupt the inference engine with a single payload. In Red Hat OpenShift AI and Red Hat AI Inference Server deployments exposing embedding or pooling models, processing negative token inputs causes an unrecoverable GPU context failure. This fault halts the entire serving process and prevents subsequent client requests from being handled until the container or process is restarted.

Ingress request validation: Configure an API gateway or reverse proxy placed in front of the model server to inspect request payloads for the `/v1/embeddings` and `/pooling` endpoints, rejecting requests where the `input` array contains negative numbers, or restricting untrusted clients to submitting text prompt strings rather than raw token lists.

notes.text: A flaw was found in urllib3. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker on the network to intercept and alter data transmitted through an HTTPS proxy. The issue occurs when target-server Transport Layer Security (TLS) settings inadvertently overwrite the proxy's TLS configuration, which can disable certificate verification on reused connection contexts. Consequently, an attacker can impersonate the proxy to monitor or modify forwarded traffic or capture client credentials.

Default Red Hat enterprise deployments that communicate directly with endpoints, utilize traditional HTTP proxies, or rely on standard CONNECT tunneling for end-to-end encryption do not expose this flaw.

This allows an attacker to exhaust network resources and overwhelm the configured authentication endpoints.

notes.text: Red Hat is aware of this vulnerability in PyJWT. Applications that reuse a mutable options dictionary across decode operations may unintentionally disable registered-claim validation.

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: For more information visit https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2026:82061

Until a fixed PyJWT version is available, create a new options dictionary for each decode() or decode_complete() call. Do not reuse a mutable options dictionary between calls with different verification settings.

vulnerabilities.title: pyjwt: pyjwt: Token validation bypass via options dictionary mutation

notes.text: A flaw was found in multidict. The multidict C extension fails to release object references during certain items-view union and subtraction operations. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying crafted input sequences to applications performing these operations, triggering uncollectable memory leaks. This issue can cause unbounded process memory growth, ultimately leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: multidict: multidict: Denial of Service via memory leak in items-view operations
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Moderate impact for Red Hat products because triggering the memory leak requires an application to evaluate specific items-view set operations against untrusted user input, which is uncommon across standard deployments. While multiple Red Hat services bundle multidict, exploitation is limited to gradual memory exhaustion and denial of service, with no possibility of remote code execution or data disclosure. Furthermore, standard dictionary access patterns, forward unions, and intersections are not susceptible to this flaw.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: For more information visit https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2026:82061

Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

notes.text: An update is now available for Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform 2.6
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform provides an enterprise framework for building, deploying and managing IT automation at scale. IT Managers can provide top-down guidelines on how automation is applied to individual teams, while automation developers retain the freedom to write tasks that leverage existing knowledge without the overhead. Ansible Automation Platform makes it possible for users across an organization to share, vet, and manage automation content by means of a simple, powerful, and agentless language.

For details about this release, refer to the release notes listed in the References section.

cwe.name: Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input

notes.text: A flaw was found in pyOpenSSL. The set_cookie_generate_callback callback function can be used to generate DTLS cookies. When the callback returns a cookie string or byte sequence longer than 256 bytes, a buffer overflow can be triggered due to a missing bounds checking before copying the data to a fixed-size buffer provided by the underlying OpenSSL library.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pyOpenSSL: DTLS cookie callback buffer overflow
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw is only exploitable when an application using the pyOpenSSL library provides a custom callback to the set_cookie_generate_callback function. For the buffer overflow to occur, the callback function must return a cookie string or byte sequence longer than 256 bytes, limiting the exposure of this issue. Due to these reasons, this vulnerability has been rated with an important severity.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in fflate. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted ZIP archive. This archive, when processed, can lead to an infinite loop during decompression, causing a Denial of Service (DoS) condition. This occurs because a malformed central directory entry in the ZIP archive causes out-of-bounds reads, which keeps a processing loop permanently active.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: fflate: fflate: Denial of Service via crafted ZIP archives
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This CVE describes a denial-of-service flaw in the fflate JavaScript compression library. Parsing a maliciously crafted ZIP archive via unzipSync()/unzip() triggers an infinite loop in the ZIP64 central-directory parser (z64e): a central directory entry declaring the ZIP64 size sentinel (0xFFFFFFFF) but omitting the required ZIP64 extra field causes out-of-bounds reads that keep the loop condition permanently true, consuming CPU indefinitely. Only fflate's ZIP-extraction APIs are affected; its gzip/deflate/zip-creation paths are not.

Red Hat products bundle fflate almost exclusively within web-frontend assets. Each affected component was assessed individually. Components that reach fflate only through compression-only consumers (posthog-js gzip telemetry, jsPDF zlib) never invoke the vulnerable unzipSync/z64e path and are marked not affected (vulnerable code not in the execute path). Components that bundle fflate in the vulnerable version range (through 0.8.2) where the ZIP-extraction path could not be positively excluded are marked affected. Where the vulnerable path is reachable only from client-side browser code processing same-origin assets, practical impact is limited to a self-inflicted denial of service within the user's own browser session rather than a service-level outage.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in AnyIO. A remote attacker in a privileged network position can bypass Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificate validation when connecting to internationalized domain names. This vulnerability occurs because the framework converts internationalized hostnames using an outdated encoding standard, Internationalizing Domain Names in Applications (IDNA) 2003 instead of IDNA 2008. If network traffic is redirected or intercepted, an attacker can present a legitimate certificate for the mismatched domain name, allowing them to impersonate the intended server and intercept or alter sensitive communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: anyio: AnyIO: TLS certificate spoofing via improper internationalized domain name encoding
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate severity for Red Hat products because exploitation requires an attacker to already be positioned to intercept network traffic, and the flaw only manifests when connecting to internationalized domain names containing non-ASCII characters. Within Red Hat supported environments and containerized AI components, workloads predominantly communicate using standard ASCII fully qualified domain names and internal endpoints. Because the defect does not allow remote code execution and requires a prior man-in-the-middle condition, the overall blast radius is constrained to specific redirected sessions.

notes.text: A flaw was found in AIOHTTP, an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to perform HTTP request smuggling due to an edge case in the WebSocket upgrade procedure. When a WebSocket upgrade request includes a body, the parser may switch protocols before the entire body is received. This leaves trailing data to be processed incorrectly, potentially enabling an attacker to bypass security mechanisms or gain unauthorized access to resources.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: aiohttp: AIOHTTP: HTTP Request Smuggling via WebSocket Upgrade
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact. This vulnerability in aiohttp's HTTP parser enables request smuggling when the server-side component handles WebSocket upgrade requests containing a body. An attacker could exploit an edge case during protocol switching, causing trailing data to be processed as subsequent requests or upgraded protocol data. This affects Red Hat products utilizing aiohttp in a server-side capacity.

notes.text: A path traversal vulnerability was found in pulpcore. The content upload API accepts a 'file_url' parameter that allows users with file repository privileges to specify a local file URL for Pulp to download and store. A URL scheme validation check uses a string prefix comparison that only rejects URLs beginning with 'file://', but Python's URL parser recognizes the 'file:' scheme without double slashes, creating a mismatch between what is validated and what is dispatched to the file downloader. An authenticated user with low-privilege repository permissions can supply a specially crafted URL using relative path traversal sequences to read any file accessible to the Pulp server process. In deployments that include Pulp Container, successful exploitation allows an attacker to read the container registry token signing private key and forge bearer tokens, granting unauthorized access to all private container repositories in the affected registry.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pulpcore: pulpcore: file:// scheme allowlist bypass in content upload file_url field enables arbitrary file read and Pulp Container registry signing key theft
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Critical severity because a low-privilege authenticated Pulp user can read arbitrary files accessible to the Pulp service process, and in deployments with Pulp Container can steal the registry JWT signing private key and forge bearer tokens granting unauthorized read and write access to private container repositories owned by other users. Red Hat product impact analysis is pending to determine which products ship the affected pulpcore code with the file_url content upload feature enabled and the Pulp Container plugin installed.

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

notes.text: A flaw was found in Ansible Operator Plugins. A low-privileged Kubernetes user can exploit a Jinja2 template injection vulnerability by crafting malicious custom resource (CR) specification values. These values are processed by Ansible without proper sanitization, allowing embedded Jinja2 expressions to be executed within the operator pod. This can lead to arbitrary code execution and privilege escalation, granting the attacker control over the operator's service account with cluster-wide permissions.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: ansible-operator-plugins: Ansible Operator Plugins: Arbitrary Code Execution via Jinja2 Template Injection
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having an Important impact rather than Critical because exploitation is bounded by the prerequisite of having authenticated access to create or modify custom resources. Upon reconciliation, malicious template syntax embedded in the resource specification executes within the operator environment, exposing the service account's cluster-level privileges. In default Red Hat deployments utilizing Ansible-based operators, watched resource attributes are automatically forwarded into the runner environment without unsafe designation. Operators constructed with Go or Helm frameworks do not utilize this templating workflow and are not affected.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
Before applying this update, make sure all previously released errata relevant to your system have been applied.
For details on how to apply this update, refer to:
https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_ansible_automation_platform/2.6#Upgrade

To mitigate this vulnerability, configure the Ansible Operator watch to explicitly mark custom resource (CR) spec values as unsafe. This can be achieved by setting `markUnsafe: true` in the `watches.yaml` configuration for the affected operator. This action prevents Jinja2 template injection by ensuring CR spec fields are not evaluated as templates. A restart of the operator pod may be required for the changes to take effect.

notes.text: A flaw was found in rustls-webpki. A remote attacker, by influencing an application to parse a specially crafted Certificate Revocation List (CRL) that contains an empty `onlySomeReasons` value in its `issuingDistributionPoint` extension, could trigger a panic. This vulnerability leads to a denial of service (DoS) in applications that explicitly enable CRL revocation checking.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: rustls-webpki: rustls-webpki: Denial of Service via crafted Certificate Revocation List
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker can cause an immediate denial of service by triggering an unhandled panic in network-facing services. Exploitation requires the consuming software to explicitly enable Certificate Revocation List (CRL) validation, a capability that is disabled by default in standard rustls configurations. Applications and services that actively ingest revocation lists from untrusted endpoints face service termination, whereas environments utilizing default certificate verification workflows remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in authlib. This flaw allows a remote attacker to bypass digital signature verification and submit forged data. When processing a JSON Web Signature (JWS, a format used to verify data integrity), the deserialize_json() function marks payloads as successfully verified without validating cryptographic signatures or requiring a verification key. Consequently, an attacker can supply manipulated data that the application treats as authentic and trusted, potentially leading to unauthorized access.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Important impact for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker could bypass cryptographic signature verification and submit forged token data. Successful exploitation directly compromises identity and integrity assurances when an application processes JSON-formatted web signatures. Exposure is primarily restricted to workloads where integrated services explicitly invoke the vulnerable JSON deserialization routine rather than standard compact tokens.

notes.text: A flaw was found in urllib3. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker on the network to intercept and alter data transmitted through an HTTPS proxy. The issue occurs when target-server Transport Layer Security (TLS) settings inadvertently overwrite the proxy's TLS configuration, which can disable certificate verification on reused connection contexts. Consequently, an attacker can impersonate the proxy to monitor or modify forwarded traffic or capture client credentials.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: urllib3: urllib3: Traffic interception via HTTPS proxy TLS configuration override
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having an Important impact because a network attacker can exploit corrupted TLS validation states to impersonate an HTTPS proxy, enabling complete interception and manipulation of sensitive communications as well as client credential theft. Successful exploitation depends on specialized application architectures where outgoing requests utilize an HTTPS-capable proxy alongside customized destination TLS parameters that inadvertently override proxy verification. Default Red Hat enterprise deployments that communicate directly with endpoints, utilize traditional HTTP proxies, or rely on standard CONNECT tunneling for end-to-end encryption do not expose this flaw.

notes.text: A flaw was found in virtualenv. The generated activation scripts for shells such as bash, zsh, and fish apply improper quoting to environment and library path variables. An attacker can exploit this by providing a crafted virtual environment path containing shell metacharacters. When an unsuspecting user sources the activation script, the embedded metacharacters are executed as shell commands, leading to arbitrary code execution with the privileges of that user.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: virtualenv: virtualenv: Arbitrary code execution via crafted paths in activation scripts
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An Important severity flaw was found in virtualenv, a tool for creating isolated Python virtual environments that is bundled as a dependency in a number of Red Hat products, including Red Hat OpenShift AI, Red Hat Enterprise Linux container images, Red Hat Hardened Images, and other Red Hat-delivered components. The generated activate (bash and zsh) and activate.fish scripts place path values that were already escaped by shlex.quote inside an additional quoted context. The surplus quotes can terminate the data-only quoted run, leaving shell metacharacters within a crafted value to be parsed as shell commands: in the bash and zsh scripts a crafted virtual environment path is interpolated when a relocated environment's recorded directory is absent, and in the fish script crafted Tcl or Tk library paths are interpolated into __TCL_LIBRARY__ or __TK_LIBRARY__. When a user sources such an activation script, an attacker who controls the crafted path can execute arbitrary code with the privileges of that user. The flaw was rated Important (CVSS 3.1 score 7.8, AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), consistent with the upstream severity; exploitation requires local control of the affected path values and user interaction to source the activation script. Red Hat product relationships for this flaw are DELEGATED: the impact described above applies where vulnerable virtualenv versions are bundled, fixes are being pursued through the responsible product components, and components where virtualenv is not present in the shipped artifact are being marked not affected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in virtualenv. When fetching seed packages such as pip or setuptools during environment creation or updates, virtualenv does not verify the integrity of downloaded files against authoritative cryptographic checksums. A network attacker or compromised mirror could substitute malicious packages under expected filenames. If virtualenv caches and installs these tampered packages into subsequent environments, an attacker can achieve arbitrary code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: virtualenv: virtualenv: Arbitrary code execution via unverified downloaded seed wheels
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An Important severity flaw was found in virtualenv, a tool for creating isolated Python virtual environments that is shipped in Red Hat products and offerings including Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform, Red Hat AI offerings, and other Red Hat cloud services. When virtualenv fetches pip or setuptools seed wheels over the network, through its periodic-update mechanism or the --download option, it does not verify the downloaded files against an authoritative cryptographic checksum. A network attacker able to intercept TLS traffic, or a compromised or stale package index or mirror, could substitute a malicious wheel under the expected distribution, version, and filename. virtualenv would then cache the tampered wheel and seed it into subsequently created virtual environments, which can result in arbitrary code execution. Red Hat products that bundle virtualenv are affected where this download path can be exercised, and fixes are being pursued through the respective product release streams; a small number of bundled components were assessed as not affected because the vulnerable component is not present in them. While the upstream project's security advisory rates this issue as low severity, Red Hat rates it as Important based on the potential for arbitrary code execution in environments created from tampered seed packages.

notes.text: A flaw was found in virtualenv. An attacker can achieve arbitrary code execution by supplying specially crafted prompt values or environment configurations containing unescaped quote characters when generating Windows virtual environments. When a user executes the resulting activation script, the injected commands run with the privileges of that user.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: virtualenv: virtualenv: Arbitrary code execution via unescaped prompt in Windows activation script
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An IMPORTANT severity command injection flaw was found in virtualenv, a tool for creating isolated Python virtual environments that is shipped as a bundled dependency in Red Hat offerings such as Red Hat OpenShift AI, Red Hat Enterprise Linux UBI container images, Red Hat Hardened Images components, and Fedora/EPEL community projects. On Windows, virtualenv's BatchActivator did not escape the prompt value before writing it into the cmd.exe set "VAR=value" statement of a generated activate.bat script. An attacker who can influence the prompt value, via the --prompt option, the VIRTUALENV_PROMPT environment variable, or the corresponding configuration setting, can supply a double quote that terminates the assignment and injects arbitrary cmd.exe commands. When a user activates the generated virtual environment on Windows, the injected commands run with that user's privileges, resulting in arbitrary code execution. The vulnerability is limited to the Windows batch activation script because the injected syntax is cmd.exe-specific. Exploitation requires the attacker to influence the prompt text and a user to activate the crafted environment, so scenarios that template the prompt from untrusted input, such as CI jobs deriving prompts from branch names, are most exposed. Some Red Hat components that bundle virtualenv are not affected because the vulnerable code or the component itself is not present in the shipped versions. For the affected Red Hat and community offerings the impact is rated IMPORTANT, and because virtualenv reaches these products as a dependency, fixes are being pursued through the delegated product and community maintainers rather than a direct Red Hat security update. Red Hat scores this flaw 7.8 (CVSS:3.1) while the upstream CVEORG record scores it 7.3 (CVSS:4.0); the difference reflects differing assessments of attack complexity and required user interaction, and both scores place the flaw in the high severity range.

notes.text: A flaw was found in virtualenv. An attacker capable of influencing environment configuration or prompt settings can inject unauthorized configuration entries into the environment configuration file by providing values containing line boundaries. This flaw allows the attacker to override core settings such as the base interpreter path, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution or environment tampering when the virtual environment is executed.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: virtualenv: virtualenv: Arbitrary code execution via configuration injection in prompt values
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in virtualenv, a tool for creating isolated Python virtual environments that is bundled in a number of Red Hat offerings, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Red Hat OpenShift AI, and other layered products and containers, as well as in Fedora and EPEL community builds. Red Hat rates this flaw as having Moderate impact. virtualenv writes prompt values verbatim into the line-oriented pyvenv.cfg file, while its reader parses the file with str.splitlines() and accepts the last value for duplicate keys. An attacker who can influence prompt input -- the --prompt command-line option, the VIRTUALENV_PROMPT environment variable, or a configuration-derived value such as a CI job templating an untrusted branch name -- can inject line boundaries and additional configuration keys, including home, into the generated pyvenv.cfg. Because tooling reads home to locate the base interpreter, a consumer that trusts the file can be redirected to an attacker-selected interpreter, potentially resulting in arbitrary code execution or environment tampering when the virtual environment is used. Exploitation requires the prompt value to come from outside the operator's trust boundary: where the operator supplies the prompt directly, they already control the command line, and the effect is corruption of their own environment rather than privilege gain. This is why Red Hat assesses the impact as Moderate, while the upstream project published the advisory with low severity. Fixes for affected Red Hat products and streams are being pursued by the responsible component and product teams under delegated resolution; some community and out-of-support-scope streams will not receive an update.

cwe.name: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)

notes.text: A flaw was found in Tornado. A remote malicious server can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) when an application using the CurlAsyncHTTPClient component fetches an untrusted web address. Because the client fails to enforce limits on incoming response sizes, the attacker can return a small, highly compressed payload (a decompression bomb) that expands to an enormous size. This unbounded memory consumption exhausts system resources and crashes the application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: tornado: Tornado: Denial of Service via decompression bomb in CurlAsyncHTTPClient
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability has been rated as Important because an untrusted remote server can remotely terminate an application process through memory exhaustion without requiring credentials. By default, Tornado deploys the SimpleAsyncHTTPClient implementation, which includes built-in thresholds for decompressed and raw payload sizes and remains unaffected by this flaw. However, systems that explicitly configure CurlAsyncHTTPClient—typically enabled for custom proxy routing or advanced transport options—bypass these protections and do not enforce body size constraints. When such client applications fetch resources from compromised or malicious web endpoints, the resulting decompression bomb can consume all available system memory, leading to an immediate denial of service.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

For details on how to apply this update, refer to:
https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_ansible_automation_platform/2.6#Upgrade

Restrict outbound HTTP client requests to trusted destinations and avoid using the CurlAsyncHTTPClient backend when fetching untrusted web content.

1. Application configuration: Configure Tornado applications to utilize the default SimpleAsyncHTTPClient instead of CurlAsyncHTTPClient, provided specialized libcurl functionality (such as custom proxy configurations or specific TLS options) is not required. The default client enforces strict size boundaries on compressed and uncompressed response bodies.
2. Network egress filtering: Implement firewall rules or egress network policies to restrict outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections exclusively to verified, trustworthy endpoints, preventing the client from contacting potentially malicious third-party servers.
3. Operational controls: Ensure that user-supplied or untrusted URLs are validated, sanitized, or rejected before initiating outbound retrieval requests.

Caveats: Switching the HTTP client backend from CurlAsyncHTTPClient to SimpleAsyncHTTPClient may disrupt services that depend on libcurl-specific features. Enforcing egress filtering may block connections to unlisted external services.

notes.text: A flaw was found in fsspec. This vulnerability can lead to arbitrary code execution due to unrestricted template evaluation in the ReferenceFileSystem component. When processing filesystem reference metadata documents, template expressions are evaluated without security restrictions or sandboxing. A remote attacker can exploit this flaw by enticing a user or automated service to open a maliciously crafted reference file, resulting in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the running application.

notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform provides an enterprise framework for building, deploying and managing IT automation at scale. IT Managers can provide top-down guidelines on how automation is applied to individual teams, while automation developers retain the freedom to write tasks that leverage existing knowledge without the overhead. Ansible Automation Platform makes it possible for users across an organization to share, vet, and manage automation content by means of a simple, powerful, and agentless language.

Security Fix(es):

* automation-gateway: authorization bypass via workload identity token forgery (CVE-2026-94416)
* automation-platform-ui: proxy-addr vulnerable to IP spoofing via IPv4-mapped IPv6 trust subnet (CVE-2026-90711)
* automation-platform-ui: compression: Denial of Service via memory leak on premature response close (CVE-2026-87776)
* automation-platform-ui: fflate: Denial of Service via crafted ZIP archives (CVE-2026-45820)
* python3.12-pulpcore: file:// scheme allowlist bypass in content upload file_url field enables arbitrary file read and Pulp Container registry signing key theft (CVE-2026-90959)
* python3.12-pyjwt: Verification key substitution via unvalidated JWKS redirects (CVE-2026-102267)
* python3.12-pyjwt: Token forgery via improper Unicode byte-order mark handling (CVE-2026-102272)
* python3.12-pyjwt: Authentication bypass via empty HMAC key acceptance (CVE-2026-102266)
* python3.12-pyjwt: Authentication bypass via acceptance of DER public keys as HMAC secrets (CVE-2026-102271)
* python3.12-pyjwt: Token forgery via acceptance of public JWK containers as HMAC secrets (CVE-2026-102273)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.

For details about this release, refer to the release notes listed in the References section.

notes.text: A flaw was found in fflate. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted ZIP archive. This archive, when processed, can lead to an infinite loop during decompression, causing a Denial of Service (DoS) condition. This occurs because a malformed central directory entry in the ZIP archive causes out-of-bounds reads, which keeps a processing loop permanently active.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: fflate: fflate: Denial of Service via crafted ZIP archives
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This CVE describes a denial-of-service flaw in the fflate JavaScript compression library. Parsing a maliciously crafted ZIP archive via unzipSync()/unzip() triggers an infinite loop in the ZIP64 central-directory parser (z64e): a central directory entry declaring the ZIP64 size sentinel (0xFFFFFFFF) but omitting the required ZIP64 extra field causes out-of-bounds reads that keep the loop condition permanently true, consuming CPU indefinitely. Only fflate's ZIP-extraction APIs are affected; its gzip/deflate/zip-creation paths are not.

Red Hat products bundle fflate almost exclusively within web-frontend assets. Each affected component was assessed individually. Components that reach fflate only through compression-only consumers (posthog-js gzip telemetry, jsPDF zlib) never invoke the vulnerable unzipSync/z64e path and are marked not affected (vulnerable code not in the execute path). Components that bundle fflate in the vulnerable version range (through 0.8.2) where the ZIP-extraction path could not be positively excluded are marked affected. Where the vulnerable path is reachable only from client-side browser code processing same-origin assets, practical impact is limited to a self-inflicted denial of service within the user's own browser session rather than a service-level outage.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: For details on how to apply this update, refer to Ansible Automation Platform documentation.

There is no available mitigation for this flaw other than updating the bundled fflate library to a fixed version (0.8.3 or later). Where the application controls the input, avoid passing untrusted ZIP archives to fflate's unzip()/unzipSync() APIs.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `compression` Node.js and Express middleware. A remote unauthenticated attacker can exploit this vulnerability by repeatedly initiating and then prematurely aborting connections while compressed responses are being sent. This action prevents the zlib stream, used for compression, from being properly destroyed, leading to a memory leak. Over time, this memory exhaustion can cause the server to crash, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has rated this vulnerability as Important. A remote unauthenticated attacker can cause a denial of service by repeatedly aborting connections while compressed responses are being sent, which can lead to memory exhaustion and server termination.

notes.text: A flaw was found in proxy-addr. When an application defines trusted proxy subnets using IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses with an improper prefix length, the subnet parser fails open and erroneously treats all incoming network addresses as trusted. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this vulnerability by submitting a forged X-Forwarded-For header to spoof their client IP address. This flaw allows attackers to bypass IP-based access controls, rate limiting, and audit logging.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: proxy-addr: proxy-addr vulnerable to IP spoofing via IPv4-mapped IPv6 trust subnet
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important because unauthenticated remote attackers can spoof client IP addresses and circumvent security controls, such as rate limits or network access lists, by sending custom forwarding headers. Exploitation is contingent on application configurations that define reverse proxy trust subnets using IPv4-mapped IPv6 notation with short IPv4 prefix lengths. Environments configuring trusted proxies via canonical IPv4 CIDR blocks, hostnames, or default loopback addresses are not vulnerable to this behavior.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: For details on how to apply this update, refer to Ansible Automation Platform documentation.

To mitigate this flaw through configuration:

1. Configure trusted proxy definitions using standard IPv4 notation (such as `10.0.0.0/8`) rather than IPv4-mapped IPv6 notation.
2. If IPv4-mapped IPv6 notation is required, set the subnet prefix length to at least 97 to cover the mapped boundary (for example, specify `::ffff:10.0.0.0/104` instead of `::ffff:10.0.0.0/8`).
3. Alternatively, sanitize or strip incoming `X-Forwarded-For` headers at edge load balancers or boundary reverse proxies before passing traffic to backend applications.

Warning: Modifying application configuration files requires restarting the Node.js application service, which will temporarily interrupt service availability and active connections.

vulnerabilities.title: proxy-addr: proxy-addr vulnerable to IP spoofing via IPv4-mapped IPv6 trust subnet

notes.text: A path traversal vulnerability was found in pulpcore. The content upload API accepts a 'file_url' parameter that allows users with file repository privileges to specify a local file URL for Pulp to download and store. A URL scheme validation check uses a string prefix comparison that only rejects URLs beginning with 'file://', but Python's URL parser recognizes the 'file:' scheme without double slashes, creating a mismatch between what is validated and what is dispatched to the file downloader. An authenticated user with low-privilege repository permissions can supply a specially crafted URL using relative path traversal sequences to read any file accessible to the Pulp server process. In deployments that include Pulp Container, successful exploitation allows an attacker to read the container registry token signing private key and forge bearer tokens, granting unauthorized access to all private container repositories in the affected registry.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pulpcore: pulpcore: file:// scheme allowlist bypass in content upload file_url field enables arbitrary file read and Pulp Container registry signing key theft
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Critical severity because a low-privilege authenticated Pulp user can read arbitrary files accessible to the Pulp service process, and in deployments with Pulp Container can steal the registry JWT signing private key and forge bearer tokens granting unauthorized read and write access to private container repositories owned by other users. Red Hat product impact analysis is pending to determine which products ship the affected pulpcore code with the file_url content upload feature enabled and the Pulp Container plugin installed.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: An authorization bypass was found in the Ansible Automation Platform (AAP) gateway. The gateway API allows an authenticated administrator to create a new service key for the Controller service cluster. Because service-key creation is not restricted to the installer-provisioned provisioning path, an administrator-issued key is cryptographically indistinguishable from a legitimate one and can be used to forge a service-authentication token that impersonates the Controller service. Combined with the gateway OIDC workload-identity endpoint (enabled via FEATURE_OIDC_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_ENABLED), the attacker can drive the gateway to sign Workload Identity Tokens (WITs) for arbitrary Controller workloads. A downstream resource server such as HashiCorp Vault that trusts the gateway OIDC key will accept the forged WIT and return the AAP credentials bound to that workload, disclosing secrets beyond the attacker's authorization boundary.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: aap-gateway: aap-gateway: authorization bypass via workload identity token forgery
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: The base CVSS scores the direct technical impact of the flaw: read-only disclosure of the AAP credentials retrievable from a downstream resource server, with Scope:Changed reflecting that the impact reaches beyond the gateway's authority into that resource server. The credentials exposed are those AAP uses to automate managed infrastructure (for example cloud IAM keys, SSH private keys, or service-account credentials), so the real-world business impact of their misuse can be significant; that consequence is deployment-dependent and is not reflected in the base metrics. Administrator-created service keys persist across upgrades, so environments that ran AAP 2.5 or 2.6 should audit and revoke non-installer-provisioned service keys even if the workload-identity feature is only enabled after upgrading to 2.7.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: For details on how to apply this update, refer to Ansible Automation Platform documentation.

Audit and revoke any Controller service keys that were not provisioned by the installer; this is the most important immediate action and applies to environments upgraded from 2.5/2.6 as well. Where the integration is not required, set FEATURE_OIDC_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_ENABLED=false to disable the workload-identity endpoint. Rotate any downstream credentials (e.g. in HashiCorp Vault) that could have been retrieved via a forged workload identity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in pyjwt. A remote attacker can forge authentication tokens and bypass security controls by signing tokens with an empty key. When verifying tokens against a JSON Web Key (JWK) set that contains an empty Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) key, the library fails to enforce key-length validation. This allows an attacker to generate valid tokens carrying arbitrary claims to gain unauthorized access.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pyjwt: pyjwt: Authentication bypass via empty HMAC key acceptance
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having an Important impact for Red Hat products because successful exploitation allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to generate forged tokens with arbitrary administrative claims, completely bypassing authentication controls. The flaw is not classified as Critical because exploitation requires a specific misconfiguration prerequisite—the target environment must actively load a symmetric key set containing a blank key entry. Typical deployments running standard authentication configurations are not exposed unless an empty HMAC key definition is explicitly ingested by the application.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PyJWT. When retrieving cryptographic keys from a JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) endpoint, PyJWKClient fails to validate HTTP redirect destinations against trusted domain boundaries. A remote attacker who can influence the response of a trusted endpoint can redirect key requests to an untrusted server, allowing the client to accept forged verification keys or potentially exposing sensitive credentials.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pyjwt: pyjwt: Verification key substitution via unvalidated JWKS redirects
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important impact because improper handling of HTTP redirects during dynamic key retrieval can allow an adversary to supply forged cryptographic keys or intercept sensitive request headers. In Red Hat environments where services utilize PyJWKClient to fetch JSON Web Key Sets over the network, accepting untrusted key material may compromise token validation and authentication boundaries. Exploitation requires the target service to dynamically resolve keys via HTTP and relies on an attacker's ability to manipulate responses returned by the configured key server.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PyJWT. The library fails to identify asymmetric public keys supplied in Distinguished Encoding Rules (DER) format, inadvertently treating the public data as a shared secret in Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) operations. If an application supports both asymmetric and symmetric signing algorithms, a remote attacker knowing the public key can exploit this flaw to forge valid authentication tokens and bypass access controls.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pyjwt: PyJWT: Authentication bypass via acceptance of DER public keys as HMAC secrets
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important because an attacker can forge valid JSON Web Tokens and bypass authentication mechanisms if public cryptographic keys are mistakenly treated as shared secrets. Exploitation requires a specific application scenario where both asymmetric and HMAC algorithms are concurrently permitted during signature verification and public keys are provided in raw DER binary format. Typical Red Hat product integrations do not employ this vulnerable algorithm combination or key encoding by default, which restricts the overall attack surface in standard production environments.

notes.text: A flaw was found in pyjwt. When verifying cryptographic keys, the raw JSON Web Key (JWK) parser fails to normalize Unicode byte-order marks (BOM). In mixed-algorithm verification environments, an attacker who knows the public key can supply a key prefixed with a byte-order mark, causing the system to misidentify the public key as a shared symmetric secret. This flaw allows an attacker to forge authenticated JSON Web Tokens (JWT) and bypass authentication controls.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pyjwt: pyjwt: Token forgery via improper Unicode byte-order mark handling
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity because successful exploitation permits an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass authentication and forge valid tokens, though exploitation requires specific mixed-algorithm verification settings. In Red Hat environments, exposure is restricted to services that simultaneously allow both symmetric HMAC and asymmetric signature algorithms while parsing public keys that contain byte order marks. Workloads and services that enforce single-algorithm verification policies or utilize standard asymmetric key validation routines are not susceptible to this attack.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PyJWT. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass authentication by forging arbitrary JSON Web Tokens (JWTs). When an application allows both symmetric and asymmetric algorithms, PyJWT fails to properly validate public JSON Web Key (JWK) container representations, mistakenly accepting public key material as a symmetric Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) secret. As a result, an attacker with knowledge of the public key can generate validly signed tokens with arbitrary authenticated claims.

notes.text: Red Hat rates this vulnerability as Important because an attacker with access to a public verification key can forge cryptographic tokens to bypass authentication, allowing impersonation of privileged users and unauthorized access to protected application resources. Exploitation is limited to environments where applications concurrently permit symmetric HMAC and asymmetric algorithms while passing public key containers into validation routines.

While it can cause a crash, the impact is limited to availability, and exploitation is unlikely in real-world deployments.

notes.text: A flaw was found in SQLite's FTS5 full-text search extension. This vulnerability involves memory corruption, specifically an out-of-bounds read and a heap buffer overflow, which can be triggered by supplying a crafted database with malformed FTS5 page data. When an FTS5 MATCH query is executed against such a database, an attacker can cause process crashes, memory exhaustion, or achieve arbitrary code execution, potentially compromising the system.

notes.text: Important: This flaw in the SQLite FTS5 full-text search extension can lead to arbitrary code execution or denial of service. Exploitation requires an application to process a specially crafted SQLite database containing malformed FTS5 page data, which could occur if an attacker provides a malicious database to a vulnerable application. This risk is elevated in scenarios where applications handle untrusted SQLite database files.

notes.text: A flaw was found in SQLite, specifically within its FTS5 full-text search extension. Attackers can exploit a heap-based buffer overflow by providing a specially crafted database. This crafted database contains malicious metadata that triggers an integer underflow during FTS5 MATCH query processing. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability can lead to a crash of the application or allow for arbitrary code execution.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `tarfile.extractall()` function within Python. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted archive. This archive could bypass security filters by using a hardlink that references a symlink, allowing the symlink to be recreated outside the intended destination directory. This could lead to out-of-destination file reads or writes, potentially resulting in information disclosure or arbitrary file modification.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: python: cpython: CPython: tarfile extraction filter bypass allows escaping the destination directory
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat products that appear in dependency searches under names containing "tarfile" but that are not the CPython standard-library tarfile module are not affected by this flaw. Matches such as the Go packages under github.com/containers/image / go.podman.io/image (.../docker/tarfile and .../docker/internal/tarfile) and the Apache Camel artifacts (camel-tarfile, camel-quarkus-tarfile) are unrelated implementations in other languages and do not include the vulnerable CPython tarfile.extractall() filter logic. The separately packaged PyPI component backports-tarfile is also out of scope for this CVE as assigned: it is not the CPython stdlib module named in the advisory and this CVE tracks the interpreter-provided tarfile shipped in Red Hat python3* packages.

notes.text: A flaw was found in pip. When processing doubly-encoded package URLs from malicious package indexes, pip incorrectly handles the file paths. A remote attacker could exploit this by convincing a user to download or install a package from such an index. This could allow for files to be installed to arbitrary locations on the system, potentially leading to system compromise. This vulnerability primarily affects users utilizing the `pip download` command with the `--only-binary` option.

notes.text: A denial-of-service and resource exhaustion vulnerability exists within the `GDBus` component of GLib. The `gdbusauth` authentication mechanism fails to enforce proper length limitations on data lines read from a client. An unauthenticated local or remote attacker can exploit this lack of input validation by sending excessively long streams of data, causing the application to consume massive amounts of system memory and CPU, potentially leading to a crash or system hang.

notes.text: A flaw was found in xdgmime. A heap-based buffer overflow can be triggered in _xdg_mime_magic_parse_magic_line() in the xdgmimemagic.c file on little-endian systems when an attacker-controlled MIME magic file in a user-writable XDG data location (e.g., in the $XDG_DATA_HOME/mime/magic path) is parsed by an application performing MIME type detection (e.g., via g_content_type_guess()). When performing byte-swap, incorrect pointer arithmetic on the write side causes an out-of-bounds write of 2 bytes, resulting in an application crash or memory corruption.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: xdgmime: heap-based buffer overflow in _xdg_mime_magic_parse_magic_line() in xdgmimemagic.c
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this issue, an attacker must convince a user to install a malicious MIME magic file in a user-writable XDG data location (e.g., in the $XDG_DATA_HOME/mime/magic path) and process it with an application performing MIME type detection, limiting its exposure. Also, only little-endian systems are vulnerable. Due to these reasons, this issue has been rated with a moderate severity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in oauthlib. When JSON with Padding (JSONP) support is enabled on the token revocation endpoint, the application fails to validate user-supplied callback parameters before reflecting them into the response. A remote attacker could exploit this flaw by submitting a crafted callback value, allowing the execution of arbitrary JavaScript code within the security context of client applications consuming the response.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: oauthlib: oauthlib: Unsafe JSONP callback injection in RevocationEndpoint allows arbitrary JavaScript response generation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate impact because successful exploitation requires a non-default configuration alongside user interaction to execute injected script within the client application's origin. In typical deployments, JSONP processing is disabled by default within oauthlib, leaving standard configurations unaffected. Exposure is limited to custom services that explicitly activate JSONP handling on the token revocation endpoint and process untrusted callback inputs.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: For more information visit https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2026:82415

JSONP support on oauthlib's token revocation endpoint is opt-in and disabled by default. Deployments can mitigate this issue by not enabling it: ensure enable_jsonp=True is not passed when constructing oauthlib's RevocationEndpoint, so that user-supplied callback parameters are never reflected into JavaScript response bodies. Upstream removed the JSONP feature from RevocationEndpoint entirely in oauthlib 4.0.0.

vulnerabilities.title: oauthlib: oauthlib: Unsafe JSONP callback injection in RevocationEndpoint allows arbitrary JavaScript response generation

notes.text: A flaw was found in oauthlib. A timing side-channel vulnerability in the Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) validation process allows a remote attacker to recover secret verification codes. Because comparison operations do not execute in constant time, an attacker who has intercepted an authorization code can measure response latency differences across repeated requests to infer the expected verification code character-by-character. Successful exploitation allows the attacker to exchange the authorization code for an access token and impersonate the victim user.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: oauthlib: oauthlib: Timing attack vulnerability in PKCE code_verifier/code_challenge comparison allows authorization code recovery
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate impact because successful exploitation requires multiple stringent prerequisites, including intercepting a valid authorization code, measuring high-resolution network response times, and an OAuth server implementation that permits repeated verification attempts without revoking the code. While oauthlib facilitates PKCE validation in OAuth 2.0 deployments across Red Hat environments, the timing discrepancies are minor and highly susceptible to network noise in real-world scenarios. Consequently, extracting secret verifiers remotely presents significant practical hurdles.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in Vim, a widely used command-line text editor. This vulnerability allows a local attacker to execute arbitrary code on the system. By opening a specially crafted Python file and then triggering the omni-completion feature, the attacker can cause Vim to run malicious code from a sibling Python package. This could lead to a complete compromise of the user's system.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: vim: Vim: Arbitrary code execution via Python omni-completion
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important vulnerability in Vim that allows a local attacker to achieve arbitrary code execution. The flaw occurs when a user opens a specially crafted Python file and invokes omni-completion, leading to the execution of malicious code from a co-located Python package. This risk is present in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and other products where Vim is deployed with Python omni-completion enabled, potentially compromising the editing user's system.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: For more information visit https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2026:82415

Users can mitigate this vulnerability by disabling Python omni-completion in Vim if it is not essential for their workflow. This prevents the execution of untrusted Python code when opening hostile files. To disable this feature, ensure that the `omnifunc` option in your Vim configuration (e.g., `~/.vimrc`) is not set to `pythoncomplete#Complete` or `python3complete#Complete`. Alternatively, users should avoid invoking omni-completion (`Ctrl-X Ctrl-O`) on Python files from untrusted sources. Disabling Python omni-completion may affect Python development functionality within Vim.

vulnerabilities.title: vim: Vim: Arbitrary code execution via Python omni-completion
